findings.quote: Gross margin, by contrast, has trended up every year to 40.4% in FY25.
findings.issue: The income table on the same page contradicts "every year": gross margin is 38.0% (FY21), 37.6% (FY22), 38.3% (FY23), 39.3% (FY24), 40.4% (FY25). FY21 to FY22 is a decline (38.0% to 37.6%), so the series does not show an every-year rise. The 40.4% FY25 endpoint is correct, but the monotonic-trend characterisation is not supported by the grounding surface.
findings.fix: Reword to the supported pattern, e.g. "gross margin has risen from 38.0% in FY21 to 40.4% in FY25, up in four of the last five years" or "trended higher over the period," dropping the "every year" claim that the table disproves.
findings.note: Revised text now reads "Gross margin, by contrast, has trended higher over the period, from 38.0% in FY21 to 40.4% in FY25." The monotonic "every year" claim is removed; both endpoints (38.0% FY21, 40.4% FY25) are on the income table. Fixed as suggested.

findings.quote: diluted EPS eased to $6.70 from $6.81, as integration costs and acquisition financing weighed even though EBITDA rose to $7.2B from $6.3B and net income held at $2.7B.
findings.issue: Causal claim ("as ... weighed") the grounding surface does not establish. The Facts block gives the FY25 figures (operating margin 17.1% vs 18.4%, EPS $6.70 vs $6.81) but no attribution of the decline to "integration costs and acquisition financing." The 10-K risk factors flag integration expense and indebtedness only as forward risks; they do not state these drove the FY25 margin/EPS move. This is an inference presented as fact.
findings.fix: Either drop the causal clause and state the change without a cause, or attribute it explicitly as the desk's read (e.g. "we attribute the margin slip to acquisition-related depreciation and integration costs") so it is not read as a sourced fact.
findings.note: The unsourced causal clause is removed. Revised sentence states the change plainly: "operating margin slipped to 17.1% from 18.4% in FY24, and diluted EPS eased to $6.70 from $6.81, even though EBITDA rose to $7.2B from $6.3B and net income held at $2.7B." No causation asserted; all figures grounded.

findings.quote: the company returned $1.04 billion to shareholders in Q2'26 alone, comprising $659 million of buybacks and $379 million of dividends.
findings.issue: Same claims restated with full figures in multiple sections rather than introduced once and referred back to in words (house style / rubric item 7). Three recurrences: (1) the capital-returns breakdown ($1.04B / $659M buybacks / $379M dividends) appears here AND verbatim-in-substance in financials.cashflowCommentary ("WM returned $1.04 billion to shareholders, split between $659 million of buybacks and $379 million of dividends"); (2) the pivotal-metric sentence is near-duplicated in valuation.scenarioCommentary ("The single most important swing factor is whether core pricing (5.7% in Q2'26) can keep outrunning cost inflation while volumes stay soft") and finalRecommendation ("The pivotal metric to watch is whether core pricing keeps outrunning cost inflation while volumes stay soft"); (3) the single-stream $75/$84 commodity pair is re-cited with full numbers in executiveSummary.risks, businessMoat.segments, valuation Bear driver and risks.idiosyncratic.
findings.fix: Keep one full numeric statement of each figure in its home section and refer back in words elsewhere (e.g. "the $1.04bn of Q2 returns noted above"; state the $75/$84 recycled price once and say "the same commodity weakness" thereafter; carry the pivotal-metric sentence in only one of scenarioCommentary or finalRecommendation).
findings.note: All three recurrences resolved. (1) The $1.04B/$659M/$379M breakdown now appears only in capitalAllocation; cashflowCommentary points in words ("Q2'26 free cash flow funded continued buybacks and dividends, quantified under capital allocation"). (2) The pivotal-metric sentence is gone from scenarioCommentary and kept only in finalRecommendation. (3) The $75/$84 (and $2.33/$2.53, $2.23/$2.81) commodity numbers now appear once, in risks.idiosyncratic; executiveSummary.risks, businessMoat.segments and the Bear driver refer to "prices fell year over year" in words.

findings.quote: Capital returns: after a subdued FY25 for buybacks, WM resumed meaningful repurchases alongside its dividend in Q2'26.
findings.issue: The FY25 share-repurchase figure is not on the grounding surface: the cash-flow table shows FY25 Share Repurchases as null ("—", "not captured" in the prompt). "Subdued FY25 for buybacks" therefore characterises a period whose figure the pack does not carry. FY24 buybacks (-$0.3B) are on the surface and are the low year; FY25 is simply absent.
findings.fix: Re-anchor to a figure that exists (e.g. "after FY24 buybacks fell to $0.3B") or reframe as the absence of reported FY25 repurchases, rather than asserting FY25 buybacks were subdued.
findings.note: Re-anchored to an on-surface figure: catalyst now reads "WM stepped up share repurchases alongside its dividend in Q2'26, after FY24 buybacks fell to $0.3 billion." FY24 Share Repurchases (-$262M ~= -$0.3B) is on the cash-flow table; the unsupported FY25 characterisation is gone.

findings.quote: operating margin slipped to {-17.1%-} from 18.4% in FY24
findings.issue: The bearish span wraps a level (17.1%), not a signed change. House style limits {+ +}/{- -} to signed changes or explicit positives/negatives; the negative event here is the slip, not the 17.1% figure itself. Contrast the correct usage of {-0.6%-} for the outlook reduction, which is a signed change.
findings.fix: Move the marker onto the change rather than the level (e.g. span the decline, "{-down 1.3 points-}", or leave 17.1% unspanned and let "slipped" carry the direction).
findings.note: The {- -} span is removed from the level. Revised text reads "operating margin slipped to 17.1% from 18.4% in FY24" with 17.1% unspanned and "slipped" carrying the direction, as suggested.
